text:
…the great wheel-holder Chödrak Palzangpo, an Indian manuscript came to hand, and, relying on his urging by command, "Fill in what is missing and complete the ending":
in the tenth bampo, from "accomplishes all the aims of the rites" up to "by the supreme recitation of secret mantra"; and
in the twelfth bampo, from "Bhagavan, nevertheless, for the sake of a special purpose" up to "the body of the vidyā-mantra holder will blaze"; and in the thirteenth bampo, from "merely by hearing this maṇḍala rite" up to "one should carve it to the size of a man"; and in the fourteenth bampo, from "having recited over lotus, water, and white mustard" up to "one should wash with white cloth, and seven times"; and at the juncture of the fourteenth and fifteenth bampos, from "eight [unclear] of silver" up to "in all other places, one performs all actions just as one intends"; and
